\section*{Question 5}

Let \(g\) be the function given by \(g(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the average value of \(g\) on the closed interval \([1,4]\).
\item[(b)] Let \(S\) be the solid generated when the region bounded by the graph of \(y=g(x)\), the vertical lines \(x=1\) and \(x=4\), and the \(x\)-axis is revolved about the \(x\)-axis. Find the volume of \(S\).
\item[(c)] For the solid \(S\), given in part (b), find the average value of the areas of the cross sections perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis.
\item[(d)] The average value of a function \(f\) on the unbounded interval \([a, \infty)\) is defined to be \(\lim _{b \rightarrow \infty}\left[\frac{\int_{a}^{b} f(x) d x}{b-a}\right]\). Show that the improper integral \(\int_{4}^{\infty} g(x) d x\) is divergent, but the average value of \(g\) on the interval \([4, \infty)\) is finite.
\item[(a)] \(\frac{1}{3} \int_{1}^{4} \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} d x=\left.\frac{1}{3} \cdot 2 \sqrt{x}\right|_{1} ^{4}=\frac{4}{3}-\frac{2}{3}=\frac{2}{3}\)
\item[(b)] Volume \(=\pi \int_{1}^{4} \frac{1}{x} d x=\left.\pi \ln x\right|_{1} ^{4}=\pi \ln 4\)
\item[(c)] The cross section at \(x\) has area \(\pi\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)^{2}=\frac{\pi}{x}\) Average value \(=\frac{1}{3} \int_{1}^{4} \frac{\pi}{x} d x=\frac{1}{3} \pi \ln 4\)
\item[(d)] \(\int_{4}^{\infty} g(x) d x=\lim _{b \rightarrow \infty} \int_{4}^{b} \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} d x=\lim _{b \rightarrow \infty}(2 \sqrt{b}-4)=\infty\) This limit is not finite, so the integral is divergent.
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\int_{4}^{b} g(x) d x}{b-4}=\frac{1}{b-4} \int_{4}^{b} \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} d x=\frac{2 \sqrt{b}-4}{b-4} \\
& \lim _{b \rightarrow \infty} \frac{2 \sqrt{b}-4}{b-4}=0
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{c}1: \text { integral } \\ 1: \text { antidifferentiation } \\ \text { and evaluation }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{c}1: \text { integral } \\ 1: \text { antidifferentiation } \\ \text { and evaluation }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[1] : answer
\item[4] : \(\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \int_{4}^{b} g(x) d x=2 \sqrt{b}-4 \\ 1: \text { indicates integral diverges } \\ 1: \frac{1}{b-4} \int_{4}^{b} g(x) d x=\frac{2 \sqrt{b}-4}{b-4} \\ 1: \text { finite limit as } b \rightarrow \infty\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
